;; source lambda on the right-hand side of the equality.

(defun logipedia-permutation-invert-body-s-body-value (index)
  (list 'logipedia-invert-permut-body-s (nfix index)))

(defun logipedia-permutation-invert-body-s-lambda-value (index)
  (list 'logipedia-invert-permut-body-s-lambda (nfix index)))

(defun logipedia-permutation-invert-body-s-higher-apply
    (value function natural)
  (cond
   ((and
     (true-listp value)
     (equal (len value) 2)
     (equal (car value) 'logipedia-invert-permut-body-s)
     (natp (cadr value)))
    (logipedia-permutation-invert-body-s-body-at
     (+ 1 (cadr value)) function natural))
   ((and
     (true-listp value)
     (equal (len value) 2)
     (equal (car value) 'logipedia-invert-permut-body-s-lambda)
     (natp (cadr value)))
    (if
     (equal
      (nfix natural)
      (logipedia-permutation-invert-body-s-function-at
       function (+ 1 (cadr value))))
     (+ 1 (cadr value))
     (logipedia-permutation-invert-body-s-invert-at
      (cadr value) function natural)))
   (t
    (nfix
     (logipedia-permutation-invert-body-s-raw-higher-apply
      value function natural)))))

;; predicates on the fixed higher-order value type.

(defstub logipedia-permutation-invert-body-s-source-equal-p
  (left right)

  (predicate value)
  t)

    (function natural expected)

   'logipedia-application-equality
   function
   (nfix natural)
   (nfix expected)))

(defun-sk
 logipedia-permutation-invert-body-s-application-semantics-p
 ()
 (forall (value function natural expected)
   (implies
    (and
     (natp natural)
     (natp expected))
    (iff
      (logipedia-permutation-invert-body-s-predicate-holds-p
      (logipedia-permutation-invert-body-s-application-predicate
       function natural expected)
      value)
     (equal
      (logipedia-permutation-invert-body-s-higher-apply
       value function natural)
      expected)))))

;; source equality transports every predicate on the higher-order type.

(defun-sk
 logipedia-permutation-invert-body-s-source-equal-leibniz-p
 ()
 (forall (left right predicate)
   (implies
    (logipedia-permutation-invert-body-s-source-equal-p
     left right)
    (implies
     (logipedia-permutation-invert-body-s-predicate-holds-p
      predicate left)

      predicate right)))))

(defun-sk
 logipedia-permutation-axiom-invert-permut-body-s-source-equality-p

 (forall (index)

    (natp index)
    (logipedia-permutation-invert-body-s-source-equal-p
     (logipedia-permutation-invert-body-s-body-value index)
     (logipedia-permutation-invert-body-s-lambda-value index)))))

(defun

 (implies
  (and

  (logipedia-permutation-axiom-invert-permut-body-s-source-equality-p)))

$(

  permutation.axiom_invert_permut_body_S
  (logipedia__metamath__permutation.axiom_invert_permut_body_S), catalog
  title "permutation.axiom_invert_permut_body_S": for every natural number
  n, the inverse-permutation body at successor n equals the functional that
  maps f and m to successor n when m equals f at successor n, and otherwise
  to invert_permut n f m. This file contains no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  LogInvertPermut and LogInvertPermutBody represent the fixed source
  constants of type

    NN0 -> (NN0 -> NN0) -> NN0 -> NN0.

  LogNatUnaryFunction is the full carrier NN0 -> NN0, LogNatFunctional is
  the full curried carrier (NN0 -> NN0) -> NN0 -> NN0, and
  LogNatToFunctional is the full type of both source constants. The nested
  maps-to terms retain the source lambdas over f and m. The SetMM
  conditional faithfully renders match_bool_type NN0 (S n)
  (invert_permut n f m) (eqb m (f (S n))), and n + 1 renders S n.

  Native SetMM equality is bidirectionally equivalent to connectives.equal
  here: equal_leibniz yields native equality, while native equality rewrites
  the right side to the left and refl_equal supplies source reflexivity. All
  declarations are unproved $a statement encodings; this database contains
  no $p proof declaration.
$)

$c
  LogInvertPermut LogInvertPermutBody LogNatUnaryFunction
  LogNatFunctional LogNatToFunctional
$.

log-invert-permut-syntax $a
  class ( LogInvertPermut )
$.
log-invert-permut-body-syntax $a
  class ( LogInvertPermutBody )
$.
log-nat-unary-function-syntax $a
  class ( LogNatUnaryFunction )
$.
log-nat-functional-syntax $a
  class ( LogNatFunctional )
$.
log-nat-to-functional-syntax $a
  class ( LogNatToFunctional )
$.

log-nat-unary-function-definition $a |-
  ( LogNatUnaryFunction ) = ( NN0 ^m NN0 )
$.

log-nat-functional-definition $a |-
  ( LogNatFunctional ) =
    (
      ( LogNatUnaryFunction )
      ^m
      ( LogNatUnaryFunction )
    )
$.

log-nat-to-functional-definition $a |-
  ( LogNatToFunctional ) =
    ( ( LogNatFunctional ) ^m NN0 )
$.

${
  $d f m n $.

  $( Source-signature typing hypotheses for the two fixed constants. $)
  log-invert-permut-type $e |-
    ( LogInvertPermut ) e. ( LogNatToFunctional )
  $.
  log-invert-permut-body-type $e |-
    ( LogInvertPermutBody ) e. ( LogNatToFunctional )
  $.

  logipedia-permutation-axiom-invert-permut-body-s $a |-
    A. n e. NN0
      ( ( LogInvertPermutBody ) ` ( n + 1 ) ) =
        (
          f e. ( LogNatUnaryFunction ) |->
            (
              m e. NN0 |->
                if (
                  m = ( f ` ( n + 1 ) ) ,
                  ( n + 1 ) ,
                  (
                    (
                      ( LogInvertPermut ` n )
                      `
                      f
                    )
                    `
                    m
                  )
                )
            )
        )
  $.
$}

-- Statement-only formalization of Logipedia corpus artifact permutation.bijn_fg
-- (catalog title "permutation.bijn_fg"): bounded surjectivity on the naturals
-- from zero through a fixed bound is preserved under function composition.
-- This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module bijn_fg where

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality using (_≡_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc)
open import Agda.Builtin.Sigma using (Σ)

infixr 2 _∧_
infix 4 _≤_

data _∧_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  _,_ : A -> B -> A ∧ B

data _≤_ : Nat -> Nat -> Set where
  zero≤ : {n : Nat} -> zero ≤ n
  suc≤suc : {m n : Nat} -> m ≤ n -> suc m ≤ suc n

Bijn : (Nat -> Nat) -> Nat -> Set
Bijn f n =
  (m : Nat) ->
  m ≤ n ->
  Σ Nat (\ p -> (p ≤ n) ∧ (f p ≡ m))

bijn-fg : Set
bijn-fg =
  (f g : Nat -> Nat) ->
  (n : Nat) ->
  Bijn f n ->
  Bijn g n ->
  Bijn (\ p -> f (g p)) n

% Statement-only formalization of the Logipedia corpus artifact
% permutation.bijn_fg, catalog title "permutation.bijn_fg": bounded
% surjectivity on a natural-number prefix is preserved by function
% composition. This file contains no proof.

permutation_bijn_fg: THEORY
BEGIN

  bijn(f: [nat -> nat], n: nat): bool =
    FORALL (m: nat):
      m <= n IMPLIES
        EXISTS (p: nat): p <= n AND f(p) = m

  bijn_fg_statement: bool =
    FORALL (f, g: [nat -> nat]):
      FORALL (n: nat):
        bijn(f, n) IMPLIES
          (bijn(g, n) IMPLIES
            bijn(LAMBDA (p: nat): f(g(p)), n))

  preimages in that segment and fixes Suc n, then it is surjective on the

theory bijn_n_Sn
  imports Main
begin

definition logipedia_bijn :: "(nat \<Rightarrow> nat) \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> bool"
  where
    "logipedia_bijn f n \<longleftrightarrow>
      (\<forall>m. m \<le> n \<longrightarrow> (\<exists>p. p \<le> n \<and> f p = m))"

  fixes f :: "nat \<Rightarrow> nat"
    and n :: nat
  assumes "logipedia_bijn f n"
    and "f (Suc n) = Suc n"
  shows "logipedia_bijn f (Suc n)"
  sorry

end

def transpose (i j n : Nat) : Nat :=
  if n = i then j else if n = j then i else n

open import Agda.Builtin.Bool using (Bool; false; true)
open import Agda.Builtin.Equality using (_≡_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc)
open import Agda.Builtin.Sigma using (Σ)

infixr 2 _∧_
infix 4 _≤_

data _∧_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  _,_ : A -> B -> A ∧ B

data _≤_ : Nat -> Nat -> Set where
  zero≤ : {n : Nat} -> zero ≤ n
  suc≤suc : {m n : Nat} -> m ≤ n -> suc m ≤ suc n

eqb : Nat -> Nat -> Bool
eqb zero zero = true
eqb zero (suc n) = false
eqb (suc m) zero = false
eqb (suc m) (suc n) = eqb m n

transpose : Nat -> Nat -> Nat -> Nat
transpose i j n with eqb n i
... | true = j
... | false with eqb n j
...   | true = i
...   | false = n

Bijn : (Nat -> Nat) -> Nat -> Set
Bijn f n =
  (m : Nat) ->
  m ≤ n ->
  Σ Nat (\ p -> (p ≤ n) ∧ (f p ≡ m))

bijn-transpose : Set
bijn-transpose =
  (n i j : Nat) ->
  i ≤ n ->
  j ≤ n ->
  Bijn (transpose i j) n

title: bijn_transpose
content:
% Statement-only formalization of the Logipedia corpus artifact
% permutation.bijn_transpose (catalog title "permutation.bijn_transpose"):
% swapping two natural indices bounded by n is surjective on the natural
% prefix from 0 through n. This file contains no proof.

permutation_bijn_transpose: THEORY
BEGIN

  transpose(i, j: nat): [nat -> nat] =
    LAMBDA (k: nat):
      IF k = i THEN j
      ELSIF k = j THEN i
      ELSE k
      ENDIF

  bijn(f: [nat -> nat], n: nat): bool =
    FORALL (m: nat):
      m <= n IMPLIES
        EXISTS (p: nat):
          p <= n AND f(p) = m

  bijn_transpose_statement: bool =
    FORALL (n, i, j: nat):
      i <= n IMPLIES
        (j <= n IMPLIES bijn(transpose(i, j), n))

END permutation_bijn_transpose

module eq_invert_permut where

open import Agda.Primitive using (Level; lsuc)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat)

InversePermutation : Set
InversePermutation =
  (Nat -> Nat) -> Nat -> Nat

Leibniz :
  {level : Level} ->
  (A : Set level) ->
  A ->
  A ->
  Set (lsuc level)
Leibniz {level} A x y =
  (P : A -> Set level) ->
  P x ->
  P y

module Statement
  (filter-nat-type : (A : Set) -> (Nat -> A) -> Nat -> A)
  (invert-permut invert-permut-body : Nat -> InversePermutation) where

  eq-invert-permut : Set₁
  eq-invert-permut =
    (n : Nat) ->
    Leibniz
      InversePermutation
      (invert-permut n)
      (filter-nat-type InversePermutation invert-permut-body n)

$(
  LogInvertPermut and LogInvertPermutBody represent the fixed source
  constants of type

    NN0 -> (NN0 -> NN0) -> NN0 -> NN0.

  LogNatUnaryFunction is the full carrier NN0 -> NN0, and
  LogNatFunctional is the full curried source result type

    (NN0 -> NN0) -> NN0 -> NN0.

  LogFilterNatTypeFunctional represents nat.filter_nat_type specialized to
  that result type. A predicate on LogNatFunctional is represented
  extensionally by a subset p of that carrier. Thus universal transport of
  membership from invert_permut n to the filtered invert_permut_body value is
  exactly the source definition of leibniz.leibniz at LogNatFunctional. All
  declarations are unproved $a statement encodings; this artifact adds no $p
  proof declaration.
$)

$c
  LogInvertPermut LogInvertPermutBody LogFilterNatTypeFunctional
  LogNatUnaryFunction LogNatFunctional LogNatToFunctional
$.

log-invert-permut-body-syntax $a class ( LogInvertPermutBody ) $.

$.

  class ( LogNatToFunctional )
$.

log-nat-unary-function-definition $a |-
  ( LogNatUnaryFunction ) = ( NN0 ^m NN0 )
$.

log-nat-functional-definition $a |-
  ( LogNatFunctional ) =

      ( LogNatUnaryFunction )
      ^m
      ( LogNatUnaryFunction )
    )
$.

  ( LogNatToFunctional ) =
    ( ( LogNatFunctional ) ^m NN0 )
$.

${

    (

        ( LogInvertPermut ) e. ( LogNatToFunctional )
        /\
        ( LogInvertPermutBody ) e. ( LogNatToFunctional )

        ( LogFilterNatTypeFunctional ) e.

            ( LogNatToFunctional )

$(
  Statement-only formalization of the Logipedia corpus artifact
  permutation.eq_invert_permut_body_O
  (logipedia__metamath__permutation.eq_invert_permut_body_O), catalog title
  "permutation.eq_invert_permut_body_O": the zero-indexed invert_permut body
  is Leibniz equal to the functional that returns zero after testing whether
  its natural-number argument equals the input function at zero. This file
  contains no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  LogInvertPermutBody represents the fixed source constant of type

    NN0 -> (NN0 -> NN0) -> NN0 -> NN0.

  LogNatUnaryFunction is the full carrier NN0 -> NN0, LogNatFunctional is
  the full curried carrier (NN0 -> NN0) -> NN0 -> NN0, and
  LogNatToFunctional is the full type of LogInvertPermutBody. The nested
  maps-to term retains the source lambdas over f and m. The SetMM
  conditional retains the source term match_bool_type NN0 0 0
  (eqb m (f 0)); both branches are zero exactly as in the source.

  A predicate on LogNatFunctional is represented extensionally by a subset
  p of that carrier. Universal transport of membership from
  LogInvertPermutBody at zero to the nested maps-to term is therefore exactly
  the source definition of leibniz.leibniz at the full functional type. All
  declarations are unproved $a statement encodings; this artifact adds no $p
  proof declaration.
$)

$c
  LogInvertPermutBody LogNatUnaryFunction LogNatFunctional
  LogNatToFunctional
$.

log-invert-permut-body-syntax $a
  class ( LogInvertPermutBody )
$.
log-nat-unary-function-syntax $a
  class ( LogNatUnaryFunction )
$.
log-nat-functional-syntax $a
  class ( LogNatFunctional )
$.
log-nat-to-functional-syntax $a
  class ( LogNatToFunctional )
$.

log-nat-unary-function-definition $a |-
  ( LogNatUnaryFunction ) = ( NN0 ^m NN0 )
$.

log-nat-functional-definition $a |-
  ( LogNatFunctional ) =
    (
      ( LogNatUnaryFunction )
      ^m
      ( LogNatUnaryFunction )
    )
$.

log-nat-to-functional-definition $a |-
  ( LogNatToFunctional ) =
    ( ( LogNatFunctional ) ^m NN0 )
$.

${
  $d f m p $.

  logipedia-permutation-eq-invert-permut-body-o $a |-
    (
      ( LogInvertPermutBody ) e. ( LogNatToFunctional )
      /\
      A. p e. ~P ( LogNatFunctional )
        (
          ( ( ( LogInvertPermutBody ) ` 0 ) e. p )
          ->
          (
            (
              f e. ( LogNatUnaryFunction ) |->
                (
                  m e. NN0 |->
                    if (
                      m = ( f ` 0 ) ,
                      0 ,
                      0
                    )
                )
            )
            e.
            p
          )
        )
    )
  $.
$}

-- (catalog title "permutation.eq_to_bijn"): bounded surjectivity on the
-- naturals from zero through n is preserved when two functions agree at every
-- input from zero through n. This file contains no proof.

module eq_to_bijn where

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality using (_≡_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc)
open import Agda.Builtin.Sigma using (Σ)

infixr 2 _∧_
infix 4 _≤_

data _∧_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  _,_ : A -> B -> A ∧ B

data _≤_ : Nat -> Nat -> Set where
  zero≤ : {n : Nat} -> zero ≤ n
  suc≤suc : {m n : Nat} -> m ≤ n -> suc m ≤ suc n

Bijn : (Nat -> Nat) -> Nat -> Set
Bijn f n =
  (m : Nat) ->
  m ≤ n ->
  Σ Nat (\ p -> (p ≤ n) ∧ (f p ≡ m))

eq-to-bijn : Set
eq-to-bijn =
  (f g : Nat -> Nat) ->
  (n : Nat) ->
  ((i : Nat) -> i ≤ n -> f i ≡ g i) ->
  Bijn f n ->
  Bijn g n

-- Statement-only formalization of Logipedia corpus artifact
-- "permutation.f_invert_permut" (catalog title
-- "permutation.f_invert_permut"): the recursively constructed inverse of a
-- permutation of a natural-number initial segment is a right inverse there.
-- This file contains no proof.

namespace permutation

def injn (f : Nat -> Nat) (n : Nat) : Prop :=
  forall i j : Nat, i <= n -> j <= n -> f i = f j -> i = j

def permut (f : Nat -> Nat) (n : Nat) : Prop :=
  (forall i : Nat, i <= n -> f i <= n) /\ injn f n

def invertPermut : Nat -> (Nat -> Nat) -> Nat -> Nat
  | 0, _, _ => 0
  | Nat.succ n, f, m =>
      if m = f (Nat.succ n) then Nat.succ n else invertPermut n f m

theorem f_invert_permut :
    forall (f : Nat -> Nat) (n m : Nat),
      m <= n -> permut f n -> f (invertPermut n f m) = m := sorry

end permutation

(*
  Statement-only formalization of Logipedia corpus artifact
  permutation.f_invert_permut (catalog title
  "permutation.f_invert_permut"): a bounded natural-number permutation maps
  its recursively defined inverse lookup back to every index in the bounded
  initial segment. This file contains no proof.
*)

From Stdlib Require Import Arith.PeanoNat.

Definition logipedia_permutation_injn
    (f : nat -> nat) (n : nat) : Prop :=
  forall i j : nat,
    i <= n ->
    j <= n ->
    f i = f j ->
    i = j.

Definition logipedia_permutation_permut
    (f : nat -> nat) (n : nat) : Prop :=
  (forall i : nat, i <= n -> f i <= n) /\
  logipedia_permutation_injn f n.

Fixpoint logipedia_permutation_invert_permut
    (n : nat) (f : nat -> nat) (m : nat) : nat :=
  match n with
  | O => O
  | S k =>
      if Nat.eqb m (f (S k))
      then S k
      else logipedia_permutation_invert_permut k f m
  end.

Theorem f_invert_permut :
  forall (f : nat -> nat) (n m : nat),
    m <= n ->
    logipedia_permutation_permut f n ->
    f (logipedia_permutation_invert_permut n f m) = m.
Admitted.

  recursively defined inverse-permutation value of any m in that segment

begin

definition logipedia_injn :: "(nat \<Rightarrow> nat) \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> bool"
where

| "logipedia_invert_permut (Suc n) f m =

    and n m :: nat
  assumes "m \<le> n"

-- a bounded natural-number permutation maps its recursively computed inverse
-- image of every value within the bound back to that value. This file contains
-- no proof.

module f_invert_permut where

open import Agda.Builtin.Bool using (Bool; false; true)
open import Agda.Builtin.Equality using (_≡_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; suc; zero)

infixr 2 _∧_
infix 4 _≤_

data _∧_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  _,_ : A -> B -> A ∧ B

data _≤_ : Nat -> Nat -> Set where
  zero≤   : {n : Nat} -> zero ≤ n
  suc≤suc : {m n : Nat} -> m ≤ n -> suc m ≤ suc n

equalNat : Nat -> Nat -> Bool
equalNat zero zero = true
equalNat zero (suc n) = false
equalNat (suc m) zero = false
equalNat (suc m) (suc n) = equalNat m n

invertPermut : Nat -> (Nat -> Nat) -> Nat -> Nat
invertPermut zero f m = zero
invertPermut (suc n) f m with equalNat m (f (suc n))
... | true = suc n
... | false = invertPermut n f m

Injn : (Nat -> Nat) -> Nat -> Set
Injn f bound =
  (i j : Nat) ->
  i ≤ bound ->
  j ≤ bound ->
  f i ≡ f j ->
  i ≡ j

Permut : (Nat -> Nat) -> Nat -> Set
Permut f bound =
  ((i : Nat) -> i ≤ bound -> f i ≤ bound) ∧
  Injn f bound

f-invert-permut : Set
f-invert-permut =
  (f : Nat -> Nat) ->
  (n m : Nat) ->
  m ≤ n ->
  Permut f n ->
  f (invertPermut n f m) ≡ m

  successor case returns the new endpoint when it matches and otherwise

  says that f maps the initial segment through n into itself; the second is
  injectivity on that segment. Native SetMM equality and order preserve the
  corresponding source predicates. The auxiliary $a declarations are syntax
  and a faithful definition; the final $a declaration is the unproved corpus
  statement, and this database contains no $p proof declaration.

$c LogInvertPermut $.

${
  $d f m n p $.

  log-invert-permut-definition $a |-
    ( LogInvertPermut n f m ) =
      if (
        E. p e. NN0
          ( p <_ n /\ ( f ` p ) = m )

  logipedia-permutation-f-invert-permut $a |-
    A. f e. ( NN0 ^m NN0 )

        A. m e. NN0

% Statement-only formalization of Logipedia corpus artifact
% permutation.f_invert_permut (catalog title
% "permutation.f_invert_permut"): a natural-number permutation of the
% initial segment through n maps its recursively computed inverse image of
% every m at most n back to m. This file contains no proof.

permutation_f_invert_permut: THEORY
BEGIN

  injn(f: [nat -> nat], n: nat): bool =
    FORALL (i, j: nat):
      i <= n IMPLIES
        (j <= n IMPLIES
          (f(i) = f(j) IMPLIES i = j))

  permut(f: [nat -> nat], n: nat): bool =
    (FORALL (i: nat):
      i <= n IMPLIES f(i) <= n)
    AND injn(f, n)

  invert_permut(
      n: nat,
      f: [nat -> nat],
      m: nat): RECURSIVE nat =
    IF n = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSIF m = f(n) THEN
      n
    ELSE
      invert_permut(n - 1, f, m)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE n

  f_invert_permut_statement: bool =
    FORALL (f: [nat -> nat]):
      FORALL (n, m: nat):
        m <= n IMPLIES
          (permut(f, n) IMPLIES
            f(invert_permut(n, f, m)) = m)

END permutation_f_invert_permut

environ

    NUMBERS, NAT_1, ORDINAL1, XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0, XXREAL_0, ARYTM_1,

    CARD_1;
  requirements REAL, NUMERALS, SUBSET, BOOLE, ARITHM;

begin

::$P-
theorem
  for f being Function of NAT,NAT,
      n being Nat st
    (for i being Nat st i <= n holds f.i <= n) &
    (for i,j being Nat st
      i <= n & j <= n & f.i = f.j holds i = j)
  holds
    ex r being Function of NAT,Funcs(NAT,NAT) st
      (for m being Nat holds (r.0).m = 0) &
      (for k,m being Nat holds
        (m = f.(k + 1) & (r.(k + 1)).m = k + 1) or
        (m <> f.(k + 1) & (r.(k + 1)).m = (r.k).m)) &
      (for i,j being Nat st
        i <= n & j <= n & (r.n).i = (r.n).j
      holds i = j)
proof
end;
::$P+

title: injective_invert_permut
content:
% Statement-only formalization of the Logipedia corpus artifact
% permutation.injective_invert_permut (catalog title
% "permutation.injective_invert_permut"): the recursively computed inverse
% of a natural-number permutation on the initial segment through n is
% injective on that segment. This file contains no proof.

permutation_injective_invert_permut: THEORY
BEGIN

  injn(f: [nat -> nat], n: nat): bool =
    FORALL (i, j: nat):
      i <= n IMPLIES
        (j <= n IMPLIES
          (f(i) = f(j) IMPLIES i = j))

  permut(f: [nat -> nat], n: nat): bool =
    (FORALL (i: nat):
      i <= n IMPLIES f(i) <= n)
    AND injn(f, n)

  invert_permut(
      n: nat,
      f: [nat -> nat],
      m: nat): RECURSIVE nat =
    IF n = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSIF m = f(n) THEN
      n
    ELSE
      invert_permut(n - 1, f, m)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE n

  injective_invert_permut_statement: bool =
    FORALL (f: [nat -> nat]):
      FORALL (n: nat):
        permut(f, n) IMPLIES
          injn(LAMBDA (m: nat): invert_permut(n, f, m), n)

END permutation_injective_invert_permut

-- Statement-only formalization of Logipedia corpus artifact
-- permutation.injective_transpose (catalog title
-- "permutation.injective_transpose"): swapping any two natural numbers
-- defines an injective function on the naturals. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module injective_transpose where

open import Agda.Builtin.Bool using (Bool; false; true)
open import Agda.Builtin.Equality using (_≡_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc)

eqb : Nat -> Nat -> Bool
eqb zero zero = true
eqb zero (suc n) = false
eqb (suc m) zero = false
eqb (suc m) (suc n) = eqb m n

transpose : Nat -> Nat -> Nat -> Nat
transpose i j n with eqb n i
... | true = j
... | false with eqb n j
...   | true = i
...   | false = n

Injective : (Nat -> Nat) -> Set
Injective f =
  (x y : Nat) ->
  f x ≡ f y ->
  x ≡ y

injective-transpose : Set
injective-transpose =
  (i j : Nat) ->
  Injective (transpose i j)

-- a natural-number function that is injective through a bound is recovered
-- by the recursively computed inverse at every input within that bound. This
-- file contains no proof.

module invert_permut_f where

open import Agda.Builtin.Bool using (Bool; false; true)
open import Agda.Builtin.Equality using (_≡_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; suc; zero)

data _≤_ : Nat -> Nat -> Set where
  zero≤   : {n : Nat} -> zero ≤ n
  suc≤suc : {m n : Nat} -> m ≤ n -> suc m ≤ suc n

equalNat : Nat -> Nat -> Bool
equalNat zero zero = true
equalNat zero (suc n) = false
equalNat (suc m) zero = false
equalNat (suc m) (suc n) = equalNat m n

invertPermut : Nat -> (Nat -> Nat) -> Nat -> Nat
invertPermut zero f m = zero
invertPermut (suc n) f m with equalNat m (f (suc n))
... | true = suc n
... | false = invertPermut n f m

Injn : (Nat -> Nat) -> Nat -> Set
Injn f bound =
  (i j : Nat) ->
  i ≤ bound ->
  j ≤ bound ->
  f i ≡ f j ->
  i ≡ j

invert-permut-f : Set
invert-permut-f =
  (f : Nat -> Nat) ->
  (n m : Nat) ->
  m ≤ n ->
  Injn f n ->
  invertPermut n f (f m) ≡ m

permutation_invert_permut_f: THEORY
BEGIN

    FORALL (i, j: nat):

      f: [nat -> nat],

    IF n = 0 THEN

      invert_permut(n - 1, f, m)

  MEASURE n

  invert_permut_f_statement: bool =
    FORALL (f: [nat -> nat]):
      FORALL (n, m: nat):
        m <= n IMPLIES
          (injn(f, n) IMPLIES
            invert_permut(n, f, f(m)) = m)

END permutation_invert_permut_f

-- Statement-only formalization of Logipedia corpus artifact
-- permutation.permut_S_to_permut_transpose (catalog title
-- "permutation.permut_S_to_permut_transpose"): a bounded permutation through
-- suc m remains a bounded permutation through m after transposing the output
-- values f (suc m) and suc m. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module permut_S_to_permut_transpose where

open import Agda.Builtin.Bool using (Bool; false; true)
open import Agda.Builtin.Equality using (_≡_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc)

infixr 2 _∧_
infix 4 _≤_

data _∧_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  _,_ : A -> B -> A ∧ B

data _≤_ : Nat -> Nat -> Set where
  zero≤ : {n : Nat} -> zero ≤ n
  suc≤suc : {m n : Nat} -> m ≤ n -> suc m ≤ suc n

eqb : Nat -> Nat -> Bool
eqb zero zero = true
eqb zero (suc n) = false
eqb (suc m) zero = false
eqb (suc m) (suc n) = eqb m n

transpose : Nat -> Nat -> Nat -> Nat
transpose i j n with eqb n i
... | true = j
... | false with eqb n j
...   | true = i
...   | false = n

Injn : (Nat -> Nat) -> Nat -> Set
Injn f bound =
  (i j : Nat) ->
  i ≤ bound ->
  j ≤ bound ->
  f i ≡ f j ->
  i ≡ j

Permut : (Nat -> Nat) -> Nat -> Set
Permut f bound =
  ((i : Nat) -> i ≤ bound -> f i ≤ bound) ∧
  Injn f bound

permut-S-to-permut-transpose : Set
permut-S-to-permut-transpose =
  (f : Nat -> Nat) ->
  (m : Nat) ->
  Permut f (suc m) ->
  Permut
    (\ n -> transpose (f (suc m)) (suc m) (f n))
    m

  Statement-only formalization of Logipedia corpus artifact
  permutation.permut_invert_permut, catalog title
  "permutation.permut_invert_permut": the recursively defined inverse of a
  natural-number function that permutes the initial segment from zero through
  n also permutes that segment. This file contains no proof.
*)

theory permut_invert_permut
  imports Main
begin

definition logipedia_injn :: "(nat \<Rightarrow> nat) \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> bool"
where
  "logipedia_injn f n \<longleftrightarrow>
    (\<forall>i j :: nat.
      i \<le> n \<longrightarrow> j \<le> n \<longrightarrow>
      f i = f j \<longrightarrow> i = j)"

definition logipedia_permut :: "(nat \<Rightarrow> nat) \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> bool"
where
  "logipedia_permut f n \<longleftrightarrow>
    (\<forall>i :: nat. i \<le> n \<longrightarrow> f i \<le> n) \<and>
    logipedia_injn f n"

fun logipedia_invert_permut ::
  "nat \<Rightarrow> (nat \<Rightarrow> nat) \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> nat"
where
  "logipedia_invert_permut 0 f m = 0"
| "logipedia_invert_permut (Suc n) f m =
    (if m = f (Suc n) then Suc n else logipedia_invert_permut n f m)"

theorem permut_invert_permut:
  fixes f :: "nat \<Rightarrow> nat"
    and n :: nat
  assumes "logipedia_permut f n"
  shows "logipedia_permut (logipedia_invert_permut n f) n"
  sorry

end

;; Statement-only formalization of Logipedia corpus artifact
;; permutation.permut_invert_permut, catalog title
;; "permutation.permut_invert_permut": the bounded inverse of a permutation
;; of the natural numbers through n is itself a permutation through n. This
;; file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

;; This unconstrained function symbol represents the source's universally
;; quantified f : nat -> nat. Its type restriction is explicit below.
(defstub logipedia-permut-invert-permut-f (x) t)

(defun-sk logipedia-permut-invert-permut-nat-function-p ()
  (forall (x)
    (implies
     (natp x)
     (natp (logipedia-permut-invert-permut-f x)))))

;; Source predicate injn: injectivity restricted to the natural interval
;; 0,...,n.
(defun-sk logipedia-permut-invert-permut-injn-p (n)
  (forall (i j)
    (implies
     (and (natp i)
          (natp j)
          (<= i n)
          (<= j n)
          (equal
           (logipedia-permut-invert-permut-f i)
           (logipedia-permut-invert-permut-f j)))
     (equal i j))))

;; Source predicate permut: f maps 0,...,n into itself and is injective there.
(defun-sk logipedia-permut-invert-permut-range-p (n)
  (forall (i)
    (implies
     (and (natp i)
          (<= i n))
     (and
      (natp (logipedia-permut-invert-permut-f i))
      (<= (logipedia-permut-invert-permut-f i) n)))))

(defun logipedia-permut-invert-permut-permut-p (n)
  (and
   (logipedia-permut-invert-permut-range-p n)
   (logipedia-permut-invert-permut-injn-p n)))

;; Source invert_permut scans indices downward: at zero it returns zero; at
;; a positive bound it returns that bound when f maps it to m, and otherwise
;; continues at the predecessor bound.
(defun logipedia-permut-invert-permut-inverse (n m)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix n)))
  (if (zp n)
      0
    (if (equal
         m
         (logipedia-permut-invert-permut-f n))
        n
      (logipedia-permut-invert-permut-inverse (- n 1) m))))

(defun-sk logipedia-permut-invert-permut-inverse-injn-p (n)
  (forall (i j)
    (implies
     (and (natp i)
          (natp j)
          (<= i n)
          (<= j n)
          (equal
           (logipedia-permut-invert-permut-inverse n i)
           (logipedia-permut-invert-permut-inverse n j)))
     (equal i j))))

(defun-sk logipedia-permut-invert-permut-inverse-range-p (n)
  (forall (i)
    (implies
     (and (natp i)
          (<= i n))
     (and
      (natp
       (logipedia-permut-invert-permut-inverse n i))
      (<=
       (logipedia-permut-invert-permut-inverse n i)
       n)))))

(defun logipedia-permut-invert-permut-inverse-permut-p (n)
  (and
   (logipedia-permut-invert-permut-inverse-range-p n)
   (logipedia-permut-invert-permut-inverse-injn-p n)))

(defun-sk logipedia-permutation-permut-invert-permut-statement ()
  (forall (n)
    (implies
     (and
      (natp n)
      (logipedia-permut-invert-permut-nat-function-p)
      (logipedia-permut-invert-permut-permut-p n))
     (logipedia-permut-invert-permut-inverse-permut-p n))))

-- Statement-only formalization of Logipedia corpus artifact
-- permutation.permut_invert_permut (catalog title
-- "permutation.permut_invert_permut"): the recursively computed inverse of a
-- bounded natural-number permutation is a permutation within the same bound.
-- This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module permut_invert_permut where

open import Agda.Builtin.Bool using (Bool; false; true)
open import Agda.Builtin.Equality using (_≡_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; suc; zero)

infixr 2 _∧_
infix 4 _≤_

data _∧_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  _,_ : A -> B -> A ∧ B

data _≤_ : Nat -> Nat -> Set where
  zero≤   : {n : Nat} -> zero ≤ n
  suc≤suc : {m n : Nat} -> m ≤ n -> suc m ≤ suc n

equalNat : Nat -> Nat -> Bool
equalNat zero zero = true
equalNat zero (suc n) = false
equalNat (suc m) zero = false
equalNat (suc m) (suc n) = equalNat m n

invertPermut : Nat -> (Nat -> Nat) -> Nat -> Nat
invertPermut zero f m = zero
invertPermut (suc n) f m with equalNat m (f (suc n))
... | true = suc n
... | false = invertPermut n f m

Injn : (Nat -> Nat) -> Nat -> Set
Injn f bound =
  (i j : Nat) ->
  i ≤ bound ->
  j ≤ bound ->
  f i ≡ f j ->
  i ≡ j

Permut : (Nat -> Nat) -> Nat -> Set
Permut f bound =
  ((i : Nat) -> i ≤ bound -> f i ≤ bound) ∧
  Injn f bound

permut-invert-permut : Set
permut-invert-permut =
  (f : Nat -> Nat) ->
  (n : Nat) ->
  Permut f n ->
  Permut (invertPermut n f) n

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  NN0 and ( NN0 ^m NN0 ) preserve the source natural-number and total
  endofunction domains. LogInvertPermut n f m is the greatest p at most n
  with f(p) = m, defaulting to zero when there is no such p. This is exactly
  the source recursive invert_permut: its zero case returns zero, and its
  successor case returns the new endpoint when it matches and otherwise
  retains the preceding result.

  Each occurrence of permutation.permut is unfolded as closure on the
  inclusive initial segment through n together with injectivity on that
  segment. Restricted quantifiers, implications, conjunctions, native SetMM
  equality, and native order preserve the source binders, assumptions, and
  conclusion. The auxiliary $a declarations are syntax and a faithful
  definition; the final $a declaration is the unproved corpus statement,
  and this database contains no $p proof declaration.
$)

$c LogInvertPermut $.

log-invert-permut-syntax $a class ( LogInvertPermut n f m ) $.

${
  $d f m n p $.

  log-invert-permut-definition $a |-
    ( LogInvertPermut n f m ) =
      if (
        E. p e. NN0
          ( p <_ n /\ ( f ` p ) = m )
        ,
        sup (
          { p e. NN0 | ( p <_ n /\ ( f ` p ) = m ) }
          ,
          NN0
          ,
          <
        )
        ,
        0
      )
  $.
$}

${
  $d f i j n $.

  logipedia-permutation-permut-invert-permut $a |-
    A. f e. ( NN0 ^m NN0 )
      A. n e. NN0
        (
          (
            (
              A. i e. NN0
                (
                  i <_ n
                  ->
                  ( f ` i ) <_ n
                )
            )
            /\
            A. i e. NN0
              A. j e. NN0
                (
                  i <_ n
                  ->
                  (
                    j <_ n
                    ->
                    (
                      ( f ` i ) = ( f ` j )
                      ->
                      i = j
                    )
                  )
                )
          )
          ->
          (
            (
              A. i e. NN0
                (
                  i <_ n
                  ->
                  ( LogInvertPermut n f i ) <_ n
                )
            )
            /\
            A. i e. NN0
              A. j e. NN0
                (
                  i <_ n
                  ->
                  (
                    j <_ n
                    ->
                    (
                      ( LogInvertPermut n f i ) =
                        ( LogInvertPermut n f j )
                      ->
                      i = j
                    )
                  )
                )
          )
        )
  $.
$}

% Statement-only formalization of the Logipedia corpus artifact
% permutation.permut_invert_permut (catalog title
% "permutation.permut_invert_permut"): the recursively computed inverse of
% a natural-number permutation on the initial segment through n is also a
% permutation on that segment. This file contains no proof.

permutation_permut_invert_permut: THEORY
BEGIN

  injn(f: [nat -> nat], n: nat): bool =
    FORALL (i, j: nat):
      i <= n IMPLIES
        (j <= n IMPLIES
          (f(i) = f(j) IMPLIES i = j))

  permut(f: [nat -> nat], n: nat): bool =
    (FORALL (i: nat):
      i <= n IMPLIES f(i) <= n)
    AND injn(f, n)

  invert_permut(
      n: nat,
      f: [nat -> nat],
      m: nat): RECURSIVE nat =
    IF n = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSIF m = f(n) THEN
      n
    ELSE
      invert_permut(n - 1, f, m)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE n

  permut_invert_permut_statement: bool =
    FORALL (f: [nat -> nat]):
      FORALL (n: nat):
        permut(f, n) IMPLIES
          permut(
            LAMBDA (m: nat): invert_permut(n, f, m),
            n)

END permutation_permut_invert_permut

-- "permutation.permut_to_bijn" (catalog title "permutation.permut_to_bijn"):
-- every natural-number function that maps an initial segment into itself and
-- is injective there is surjective on that initial segment.
-- This file contains no proof.

namespace permutation

def injn (f : Nat → Nat) (n : Nat) : Prop :=
  ∀ i j : Nat, i ≤ n → j ≤ n → f i = f j → i = j

def permut (f : Nat → Nat) (n : Nat) : Prop :=
  (∀ i : Nat, i ≤ n → f i ≤ n) ∧ injn f n

def bijn (f : Nat → Nat) (n : Nat) : Prop :=

theorem permut_to_bijn :
    ∀ (n : Nat) (f : Nat → Nat), permut f n → bijn f n := sorry

end permutation

permut-to-bijn : Set

title: permut_to_bijn
content:
% Statement-only formalization of the Logipedia corpus artifact
% permutation.permut_to_bijn, catalog title "permutation.permut_to_bijn":
% a function that maps a natural-number prefix into itself and is injective
% there is surjective onto that prefix. This file contains no proof.

permutation_permut_to_bijn: THEORY
BEGIN

  injn(f: [nat -> nat], n: nat): bool =
    FORALL (i, j: nat):
      i <= n IMPLIES
        (j <= n IMPLIES
          (f(i) = f(j) IMPLIES i = j))

  permut(f: [nat -> nat], n: nat): bool =
    (FORALL (i: nat):
      i <= n IMPLIES f(i) <= n)
    AND injn(f, n)

  bijn(f: [nat -> nat], n: nat): bool =
    FORALL (m: nat):
      m <= n IMPLIES
        EXISTS (p: nat):
          p <= n AND f(p) = m

  permut_to_bijn_statement: bool =
    FORALL (n: nat):
      FORALL (f: [nat -> nat]):
        permut(f, n) IMPLIES bijn(f, n)

END permutation_permut_to_bijn

$(

  LogNatUnaryFunction is the full carrier NN0 -> NN0, LogNatFunctional is
  the full curried carrier (NN0 -> NN0) -> NN0 -> NN0, and
  LogNatToFunctional is the full type of both source constants. The nested

  maps-to term to LogInvertPermutBody at successor n is therefore exactly

% Statement-only formalization of Logipedia corpus artifact
% permutation.sym_eq_invert_permut_body_S (catalog title

% index, the curried function that returns that successor when the input
% matches the function's value there, and otherwise returns the preceding
% inverse-permutation result, is Leibniz-equal to the inverse-permutation
% body. This file contains no proof.

permutation_sym_eq_invert_permut_body_S: THEORY
BEGIN
  invert_permut, invert_permut_body: [nat -> [[nat -> nat] -> [nat -> nat]]]
  inverse_permutation_function: TYPE =
    [[nat -> nat] -> [nat -> nat]]

  leibniz(x: inverse_permutation_function)
         (y: inverse_permutation_function): bool =
    FORALL (P: [inverse_permutation_function -> bool]):
      P(x) IMPLIES P(y)

  sym_eq_invert_permut_body_S_statement: bool =
    FORALL (n: nat):
      leibniz
        (LAMBDA (f: [nat -> nat]):
          (LAMBDA (m: nat):
            IF m = f(n + 1)
            THEN n + 1
            ELSE invert_permut(n)(f)(m)
            ENDIF))
        (invert_permut_body(n + 1))
END permutation_sym_eq_invert_permut_body_S

    (index dividend divisor)

leb : Nat -> Nat -> Bool

-- Statement-only formalization of Logipedia corpus artifact
-- relations.RC_reflexive (catalog title "relations.RC_reflexive"): adjoining
-- equality to an arbitrary binary relation yields a reflexive relation.
-- This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module RC_reflexive where

open import Agda.Primitive using (Level; lsuc; _⊔_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Equality using (_≡_)

infixr 2 _∨_

data _∨_ {p q : Level} (P : Set p) (Q : Set q) : Set (p ⊔ q) where
  left : P -> P ∨ Q
  right : Q -> P ∨ Q

Reflexive :
  {a r : Level} {A : Set a} ->
  (A -> A -> Set r) ->
  Set (a ⊔ r)
Reflexive {A = A} relation =
  (x : A) -> relation x x

RC :
  {a r : Level} {A : Set a} ->
  (A -> A -> Set r) ->
  A ->
  A ->
  Set (a ⊔ r)
RC relation x y =
  relation x y ∨ x ≡ y

relations-RC-reflexive :
  {a r : Level} ->
  Set (lsuc a ⊔ lsuc r)
relations-RC-reflexive {a} {r} =
  (A : Set a) ->
  (R : A -> A -> Set r) ->
  Reflexive (RC R)

$(
  A SetMM set h represents the arbitrary source type A, and
  r e. ~P ( h X. h ) ranges over every binary relation R on A. The source
  definitions unfold as

    reflexive A (RC A R)
      = forall x : A, connectives.Or (R x x) (logic.eq A x x).

  Relation application is represented by ordered-pair membership. SetMM's
  native disjunction is bidirectionally equivalent to connectives.Or:
  or_introl and or_intror give the reverse direction, while match_Or_prop
  gives the forward direction by eliminating into native disjunction.
  SetMM equality is likewise bidirectionally equivalent to logic.eq:
  logic.refl gives native-equality substitution into logic.eq, while logic.eq_ind
  with the predicate z |-> x = z sends logic.eq A x y to x = y.

  Thus the final $a declaration is the direct native rendering of the unfolded
  source proposition. It is Metamath's unproved statement encoding; this
  database contains no $p proof declaration.
$)

${
  $d h r x $.

  logipedia-relations-rc-reflexive $a |-
    A. h
      A. r e. ~P ( h X. h )
        A. x e. h
          ( <. x , x >. e. r \/ x = x )
  $.
$}

-- Statement-only formalization of Logipedia corpus artifact "sigma_pi.exp_pi_bc"
-- (catalog title "sigma_pi.exp_pi_bc"): distributing a constant natural factor
-- across a shifted finite product. This file contains no proof.

namespace sigma_pi

def bigop (H : Type) :
    Nat → (Nat → Bool) → H → (H → H → H) → (Nat → H) → H
  | 0, _p, nil, _op, _f => nil
  | n + 1, p, nil, op, f =>
      match p n with
      | true => op (f n) (bigop H n p nil op f)
      | false => bigop H n p nil op f

theorem exp_pi_bc (a b c : Nat) (f : Nat → Nat) :
    a ^ (c - b) *
        bigop Nat (c - b) (fun _ => true) 1 Nat.mul (fun i => f (i + b)) =
      bigop Nat (c - b) (fun _ => true) 1 Nat.mul (fun i => a * f (i + b)) := sorry

end sigma_pi

(*
  Statement-only formalization of Logipedia corpus artifact
  sigma_pi.exp_pi_bc (catalog title "sigma_pi.exp_pi_bc"): multiplying a
  shifted finite product by a natural power distributes one copy of the base
  into every factor. This file contains no proof.
*)

From Stdlib Require Import Arith.PeanoNat Bool.Bool.

Fixpoint sigma_pi_bigop {H : Type}
    (n : nat) (p : nat -> bool) (nil : H)
    (op : H -> H -> H) (f : nat -> H) : H :=
  match n with
  | O => nil
  | S k =>
      if p k
      then op (f k) (sigma_pi_bigop k p nil op f)
      else sigma_pi_bigop k p nil op f
  end.

Fixpoint sigma_pi_exp (a n : nat) : nat :=
  match n with
  | O => 1
  | S k => Nat.mul (sigma_pi_exp a k) a
  end.

Theorem exp_pi_bc :
  forall (a b c : nat) (f : nat -> nat),
    Nat.mul
      (sigma_pi_exp a (Nat.sub c b))
      (sigma_pi_bigop
        (Nat.sub c b)
        (fun _ => true)
        1
        Nat.mul
        (fun i => f (Nat.add i b))) =
    sigma_pi_bigop
      (Nat.sub c b)
      (fun _ => true)
      1
      Nat.mul
      (fun i => Nat.mul a (f (Nat.add i b))).
Admitted.

-- Statement-only formalization of Logipedia corpus artifact
-- sigma_pi.exp_pi_bc (catalog title "sigma_pi.exp_pi_bc"): the identity
-- equating a^(c - b) times a finite product over shifted natural indices with
-- the product obtained by multiplying every factor by a. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module exp_pi_bc where

open import Agda.Builtin.Bool using (Bool; false; true)
open import Agda.Builtin.Equality using (_≡_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using
  (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _-_; _*_)

one : Nat
one = suc zero

power : Nat -> Nat -> Nat
power a zero =
  one
power a (suc n) =
  a * power a n

bigop :
  {A : Set} ->
  Nat ->
  (Nat -> Bool) ->
  A ->
  (A -> A -> A) ->
  (Nat -> A) ->
  A
bigop zero predicate identity operation terms =
  identity
bigop (suc n) predicate identity operation terms with predicate n
... | true =
  operation
    (terms n)
    (bigop n predicate identity operation terms)
... | false =
  bigop n predicate identity operation terms

exp-pi-bc : Set
exp-pi-bc =
  (a b c : Nat) ->
  (f : Nat -> Nat) ->
  power a (c - b) *
    bigop
      (c - b)
      (\ _ -> true)
      one
      _*_
      (\ i -> f (i + b))
  ≡
    bigop
      (c - b)
      (\ _ -> true)
      one
      _*_
      (\ i -> a * f (i + b))

content:
% Statement-only formalization of the Logipedia corpus artifact
% sigma_pi.exp_pi_bc (catalog title "sigma_pi.exp_pi_bc"): distributing a
% constant natural factor across a shifted finite prefix product equals
% multiplication by its corresponding natural power, using truncated natural
% subtraction for the prefix length. This file contains no proof.

sigma_pi_exp_pi_bc: THEORY
BEGIN

  source_equal(left, right: nat): bool =
    FORALL (property: [nat -> bool]):
      property(left) IMPLIES property(right)

  truncated_subtraction(minuend, subtrahend: nat): nat =
    IF subtrahend <= minuend THEN
      minuend - subtrahend
    ELSE
      0
    ENDIF

  source_power(base, exponent: nat): RECURSIVE nat =
    IF exponent = 0 THEN
      1
    ELSE
      base * source_power(base, exponent - 1)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE exponent

  source_bigop(
      count: nat,
      predicate: [nat -> bool],
      nil: nat,
      op: [nat -> [nat -> nat]],
      value: [nat -> nat]): RECURSIVE nat =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      nil
    ELSIF predicate(count - 1) THEN
      op(value(count - 1))(
        source_bigop(count - 1, predicate, nil, op, value))
    ELSE
      source_bigop(count - 1, predicate, nil, op, value)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  exp_pi_bc_statement: bool =
    FORALL (a, b, c: nat), (f: [nat -> nat]):
      LET count: nat = truncated_subtraction(c, b),
          multiply: [nat -> [nat -> nat]] =
            (LAMBDA (left: nat):
              (LAMBDA (right: nat): left * right))
      IN
        source_equal(
          source_power(a, count)
            * source_bigop(
                count,
                (LAMBDA (i: nat): TRUE),
                1,
                multiply,
                (LAMBDA (i: nat): f(i + b))),
          source_bigop(
            count,
            (LAMBDA (i: nat): TRUE),

  (catalog title "sigma_pi.exp_pi_l"): multiplying a finite product of
  natural values by a natural base raised to the number of factors equals
  the product obtained by multiplying every factor by that base. This file
  contains no proof.

From Stdlib Require Import Arith.PeanoNat Bool.Bool.

Fixpoint sigma_pi_exp (a n : nat) : nat :=
  match n with
  | O => S O
  | S k => Nat.mul (sigma_pi_exp a k) a
  end.

Fixpoint sigma_pi_bigop {H : Type}
    (n : nat) (p : nat -> bool) (nil : H)
    (op : H -> H -> H) (f : nat -> H) : H :=
  match n with
  | O => nil
  | S k =>
      if p k
      then op (f k) (sigma_pi_bigop k p nil op f)
      else sigma_pi_bigop k p nil op f
  end.

Theorem sigma_pi_exp_pi_l :
  forall (n a : nat) (f : nat -> nat),
    Nat.mul
      (sigma_pi_exp a n)
      (sigma_pi_bigop n (fun _ => true) (S O) Nat.mul f) =
    sigma_pi_bigop
      n
      (fun _ => true)
      (S O)
      Nat.mul
      (fun i => Nat.mul a (f i)).
Admitted.

-- Statement-only formalization of Logipedia corpus artifact
-- sigma_pi.exp_pi_l (catalog title "sigma_pi.exp_pi_l"): multiplying a
-- length-n product of natural-valued terms by a raised to n equals the product
-- obtained by multiplying each of those terms by a. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module exp_pi_l where

open import Agda.Builtin.Bool using (Bool; false; true)
open import Agda.Builtin.Equality using (_≡_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _*_)

one : Nat
one = suc zero

power : Nat -> Nat -> Nat
power a zero =
  one
power a (suc n) =
  a * power a n

bigop :
  {A : Set} ->
  Nat ->
  (Nat -> Bool) ->
  A ->
  (A -> A -> A) ->
  (Nat -> A) ->
  A
bigop zero predicate identity operation terms =
  identity
bigop (suc n) predicate identity operation terms with predicate n
... | true =
  operation
    (terms n)
    (bigop n predicate identity operation terms)
... | false =
  bigop n predicate identity operation terms

exp-pi-l : Set
exp-pi-l =
  (n a : Nat) ->
  (f : Nat -> Nat) ->
  power a n *
    bigop
      n
      (\ _ -> true)
      one
      _*_
      f
  ≡
    bigop
      n
      (\ _ -> true)
      one
      _*_
      (\ i -> a * f i)

% (catalog title "sigma_pi.exp_pi_l"): multiplying a finite prefix product of
% natural values by a natural power equals the prefix product after multiplying
% every factor by the base. This file contains no proof.

sigma_pi_exp_pi_l: THEORY
BEGIN

  natural_power(base, exponent: nat): RECURSIVE nat =
    IF exponent = 0 THEN
      1
    ELSE
      natural_power(base, exponent - 1) * base
    ENDIF
  MEASURE exponent

  prefix_product(count: nat, value: [nat -> nat]): RECURSIVE nat =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      1
    ELSE
      value(count - 1) * prefix_product(count - 1, value)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  exp_pi_l_statement: bool =
    FORALL (n, a: nat), (f: [nat -> nat]):
      natural_power(a, n) * prefix_product(n, f)
        = prefix_product(
            n,
            LAMBDA (i: nat): a * f(i))
